label: Google Calendar
description: Arcade.dev LLM tools for Google Calendar

tools.name: CreateEvent
tools.description:
Create a new event/meeting/sync/meetup in the specified calendar.

Pass `recurrence` to create a repeating event.

parameters.name: summary
parameters.description: The title of the event

parameters.name: start_datetime
parameters.description: When the event starts. For a timed event, a datetime in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). For an all-day event, a date (YYYY-MM-DD); end_datetime must then be a date too.

parameters.name: end_datetime
parameters.description: When the event ends. For a timed event, a datetime in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). For an all-day event, a date (YYYY-MM-DD) that is exclusive: the day after the event's last day. A date equal to start_datetime creates a single all-day event on that day.

parameters.name: calendar_id
parameters.description: The ID of the calendar to create the event in. Defaults to 'primary'.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: The description of the event

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: The location of the event

parameters.name: visibility
parameters.description: The visibility of the event. Defaults to default, which uses the calendar's default visibility.

parameters.name: attendee_emails
parameters.description: The list of attendee emails. Must be valid email addresses e.g., username@domain.com.

parameters.name: send_notifications_to_attendees
parameters.description: Which guests Google emails an invitation to. externalOnly emails only guests who do not use Google Calendar. Defaults to all.

parameters.name: add_google_meet
parameters.description: Whether to add a Google Meet link to the event. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: recurrence
parameters.description: Recurrence rules for a repeating event, in RFC 5545 format. Each entry is an RRULE/RDATE/EXDATE line; a bare rule is automatically prefixed with 'RRULE:'. Examples: ['RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR;COUNT=10'] for every Mon/Wed/Fri for 10 occurrences, or ['RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;UNTIL=20241231T000000Z'] for daily until 2024-12-31. Omit for a one-time event.

output.description: A dictionary containing the created event details

description.value: Weekly team sync to discuss project updates, blockers, and upcoming milestones.

location.value: Conference Room B, 123 Main St, San Francisco, CA

tools.name: FindTimeSlotsWhenEveryoneIsFree
tools.description: Provides time slots when everyone is free within a given date range and time boundaries.

parameters.name: email_addresses
parameters.description: The list of email addresses from people in the same organization domain (apart from the currently logged in user) to search for free time slots. Defaults to None, which will return free time slots for the current user only.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: The start date to search for time slots in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Defaults to today's date. It will search starting from this date at the time 00:00:00.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: The end date to search for time slots in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Defaults to seven days from the start date. It will search until this date at the time 23:59:59.

parameters.name: start_time_boundary
parameters.description: Will return free slots in any given day starting from this time in the format 'HH:MM'. Defaults to '08:00', which is a usual business hour start time.

parameters.name: end_time_boundary
parameters.description: Will return free slots in any given day until this time in the format 'HH:MM'. Defaults to '18:00', which is a usual business hour end time.

output.description: A dictionary with the free slots and the timezone in which time slots are represented.

tools.name: GetEvent
tools.description:
Get one Google Calendar event by its id.

When the event is one occurrence of a recurring series, the series' repeat rule and first
start are returned too, so read them here before changing or ending a series. The rule
counts from series_start, not from this occurrence's start. Use this instead of
listing a time window whenever the event id is already known. Deleted events and deleted
occurrences are still returned, with a cancelled status.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the event. For a recurring event, pass an occurrence's id to read that occurrence along with its series' repeat rule, or the series id to read the series itself.

parameters.name: calendar_id
parameters.description: The identifier of the calendar that holds the event. Defaults to 'primary', the authenticated user's main calendar.

output.description: The event's details, and the repeat rule and first start of its series

tools.description: List all calendars accessible by the user.

parameters.name: max_results
parameters.description: The maximum number of calendars to return. Up to 250 calendars, defaults to 10.

parameters.name: show_deleted
parameters.description: Whether to show deleted calendars. Defaults to False

parameters.name: show_hidden
parameters.description: Whether to show hidden calendars. Defaults to False

parameters.name: next_page_token
parameters.description: The token to retrieve the next page of calendars. Optional.

output.description: A dictionary containing the calendars accessible by the end user

tools.name: ListEvents
tools.description:
List events from the specified calendar within the given datetime range.

min_end_datetime serves as the lower bound (exclusive) for an event's end time.
max_start_datetime serves as the upper bound (exclusive) for an event's start time.

For example:
If min_end_datetime is set to 2024-09-15T09:00:00 and max_start_datetime
is set to 2024-09-16T17:00:00, the function will return events that:
1. End after 09:00 on September 15, 2024 (exclusive)
2. Start before 17:00 on September 16, 2024 (exclusive)
This means an event starting at 08:00 on September 15 and
ending at 10:00 on September 15 would be included, but an
event starting at 17:00 on September 16 would not be included.

parameters.name: min_end_datetime
parameters.description: Filter by events that end on or after this datetime in ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2024-09-15T09:00:00'.

parameters.name: max_start_datetime
parameters.description: Filter by events that start before this datetime in ISO 8601 format, e.g., '2024-09-16T17:00:00'.

parameters.name: calendar_id
parameters.description: The ID of the calendar to list events from. Defaults to 'primary'.

parameters.name: max_results
parameters.description: The maximum number of events to return. Defaults to 10.

output.description: A dictionary containing the list of events

tools.description:
Accept, decline, or tentatively accept (RSVP to) a meeting invitation on the
authenticated user's behalf.

Sets the user's responseStatus for an event they were invited to.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The ID of the event to respond to. Use an event's id from an event listing to respond to a single occurrence of a recurring event, or its recurringEventId to respond to the whole series.

parameters.name: response

tools.name: UpdateEvent
tools.description:
Update an existing event in the specified calendar with the provided details.
Only the provided fields will be updated; others will remain unchanged.
Pass `updated_calendar_id` to move the event to another calendar.

An event's details can only be changed by the event's organizer, or by a guest
when the organizer has enabled guest editing for that event.

`updated_start_datetime` and `updated_end_datetime` are
independent and can be provided separately, except that all-day
dates must be provided for both.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The ID of the event to update

parameters.name: calendar_id
parameters.description: The ID of the calendar containing the event. Defaults to 'primary'.

parameters.name: updated_start_datetime
parameters.description: The updated start of the event. For a timed event, a datetime in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). For an all-day event, a date (YYYY-MM-DD); updated_end_datetime must then be a date too.

parameters.name: updated_end_datetime
parameters.description: The updated end of the event. For a timed event, a datetime in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). For an all-day event, a date (YYYY-MM-DD) that is exclusive: the day after the event's last day. A date equal to updated_start_datetime makes it a single all-day event on that day.

parameters.name: updated_calendar_id
parameters.description: The ID of a calendar to move the event to. The event is moved there after the other updates are applied. Omit to keep the event on its current calendar.

parameters.name: updated_summary
parameters.description: The updated title of the event

parameters.name: updated_description
parameters.description: The updated description of the event

parameters.name: updated_location
parameters.description: The updated location of the event

parameters.name: updated_visibility
parameters.description: The visibility of the event

parameters.name: updated_recurrence
parameters.description: Updated recurrence rules for a repeating event, in RFC 5545 format. Each entry is an RRULE/RDATE/EXDATE line; a bare rule is automatically prefixed with 'RRULE:'. Provide the full set of rules to replace the event's existing recurrence, e.g. ['RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR;COUNT=10'] for every Mon/Wed/Fri for 10 occurrences. Pass an empty list ([]) to REMOVE recurrence and make the event a one-time event. Omit (leave unset) to leave recurrence unchanged.

parameters.name: attendee_emails_to_add
parameters.description: The list of attendee emails to add. Must be valid email addresses e.g., username@domain.com.

parameters.name: attendee_emails_to_remove
parameters.description: The list of attendee emails to remove. Must be valid email addresses e.g., username@domain.com.

parameters.name: send_notifications_to_attendees
parameters.description: Which guests Google emails about the update. externalOnly emails only guests who do not use Google Calendar. Defaults to all.

parameters.name: updated_google_meet
parameters.description: Add or remove the event's Google Meet link. Defaults to None, which leaves the link unchanged.

output.description: A string containing the updated event details, including the event ID, update timestamp, and a link to view the updated event.

updated_description.value: Revised agenda: Review Q3 OKRs, discuss budget allocations, and assign action items.

updated_location.value: Conference Room B, 123 Main St, San Francisco, CA 94105

summary:
## Google Calendar Toolkit

Arcade's Google Calendar toolkit connects LLMs to Google Calendar via OAuth 2.0, enabling agents to read, create, modify, and manage calendar data on behalf of authenticated users.

## Capabilities

- **Calendar & event discovery:** List all accessible calendars, retrieve events within a datetime window using precise boundary semantics, and fetch a single event by ID (including cancelled events and recurring-series metadata).
- **Event creation & recurrence:** Create one-off or repeating events/meetings with full recurrence rule support.
- **Event modification & movement:** Update individual fields of an existing event (start/end time, details, etc.) or move it to another calendar; respects organizer-vs-guest edit permissions.
- **RSVP management:** Accept, decline, or tentatively accept meeting invitations on the user's behalf by setting their `responseStatus`.
- **Scheduling intelligence:** Find free time slots across multiple attendees within a specified date range and time boundaries.
- **User identity:** Retrieve the authenticated user's profile, email, and Calendar permission details.

## OAuth

This toolkit uses OAuth 2.0 via Google. See the [Arcade Google auth provider docs](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/references/auth-providers/google) for configuration details.
